gaps.sentence: It took him months to ___ the habit of biting his nails.
gaps.explanation: break a habit (or kick a habit) means to stop doing something you do regularly.

gaps.sentence: Smoking can ___ serious harm to your health.
gaps.explanation: do harm to something is the fixed phrase; 'make harm' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a quick shower before leaving the gym.
gaps.explanation: have a shower is the standard British English collocation; 'made a shower' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: Let me ___ a photo of you both.
gaps.explanation: take a photo/picture is the fixed collocation for photographing something.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ your word, people will trust you.
gaps.explanation: keep your word means to do what you promised.
